proposed_widenings.name: embedded_payload_inventory
proposed_widenings.justification: The robe is a finite heterogeneous stock of latent payloads. Each activation must choose one remaining patch, consume that exact patch, and release a different downstream payload. Current magic-item activation records only model a fixed phase sequence over scalar resources such as use counts or charge pools.
proposed_widenings.evidence: While wearing the robe, you can take a Magic action to detach one of the patches, causing it to become the object or creature it represents. Once the last patch is removed, the robe becomes an ordinary garment.

proposed_widenings.name: ActivationResource.embedded_inventory
proposed_widenings.justification: A scalar use counter or charge pool cannot honestly represent named per-patch stock such as two lanterns, two daggers, two ropes, plus a variable set of extra patches from a table.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The robe has two of each of the following patches ... In addition, the robe has 4d4 other patches.

proposed_widenings.name: ActivationPhase.release_embedded_payload
proposed_widenings.justification: The released payload is not a single fixed effect. Different patches become mundane objects, creatures, consumable magic items, or a spell scroll of a chosen level. That requires a release step that can dispatch to heterogeneous stored payload records instead of one fixed EffectAtom list.
proposed_widenings.evidence: causing it to become the object or creature it represents

notes: Did not author content JSON/Dhall. Magic-item kind exists, but the robe's core mechanic is a stored heterogeneous patch inventory with per-patch depletion and heterogeneous releases. The GM-chosen or random generation of the extra 4d4 patches is secondary; the main blocker is the missing stored-payload inventory shape.
